purpose: Determine whether the stage-resolved C1 diagnosis can support an engineering consequence without colliding with already-published memory-utilization methods or benchmark contributions.

frozen_current_object.scientific_object: stage-resolved transport of a controlled persistent-state contrast
frozen_current_object.current_signature: write supported; source-item exposure observed; first-action branch contrast not supported; terminal transport sparse/heterogeneous; forced capacity supported
frozen_current_object.claim_boundary: operational evidence localization only; no causal mediation coefficient and no claim that retrieval-utilization separation itself is novel

published_nearest_work.work: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
published_nearest_work.overlap: success/failure-derived persistent reasoning memory and reuse
published_nearest_work.residual: does not make C1's same-trajectory stage-transport identification or stage-indexed credit rule redundant

published_nearest_work.work: How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
published_nearest_work.overlap: empirical memory dynamics, error propagation, addition/deletion choices, and practical memory-management guidance
published_nearest_work.collision_risk: HIGH if C1 claims generic memory-quality management or future-task evaluation as a new idea
published_nearest_work.residual: C1 intervenes on the same source trajectory and asks how a treatment-induced persistent-state contrast is transported across write/exposure/uptake/outcome surfaces

published_nearest_work.work: Mem2ActBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Memory Utilization in Task-Oriented Autonomous Agents
published_nearest_work.overlap: retrieving memory is insufficient; active memory application should be measured in task-oriented action execution
published_nearest_work.collision_risk: HIGH if C1 claims retrieval-versus-use as its novelty
published_nearest_work.residual: C1 traces a controlled persistent-state intervention across multiple causal/evaluation surfaces and contrasts native transport with forced downstream capacity

published_nearest_work.work: MemCoRL: Alternating Co-Optimization of Memory Retrieval and Utilization via Collaborative Reinforcement Learning
published_nearest_work.overlap: explicitly separates retrieval and utilization and optimizes both
published_nearest_work.collision_risk: FATAL if C1 is reframed as a generic retrieval-utilization optimization method
published_nearest_work.residual: C1 may use a utilization-side intervention only as a diagnostic-guided repair probe; method novelty must remain stage-resolved identification/credit, not generic utilization optimization

published_nearest_work.work: Chain-of-Memory: Lightweight Memory Construction with Dynamic Evolution for LLM Agents
published_nearest_work.overlap: identifies a retrieval-recall versus reasoning-accuracy gap and proposes a stronger utilization mechanism
published_nearest_work.collision_risk: FATAL if C1's engineering contribution is merely better post-retrieval reasoning
published_nearest_work.residual: C1 asks when a controlled self-improvement update has earned behavioral credit and whether its diagnosis predicts the repair surface

published_nearest_work.work: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
published_nearest_work.collision_risk: MEDIUM for broad memory-management method claims
published_nearest_work.residual: C1 is a measurement/identification contribution with a bounded diagnostic-guided repair test rather than a learned manager

published_nearest_work.work: Controllable Memory Usage: Balancing Anchoring and Innovation in Long-Term Human-Agent Interaction
published_nearest_work.overlap: behavioral memory dependence and control of memory reliance
published_nearest_work.collision_risk: MEDIUM if C1 claims generic memory-dependence measurement/control
published_nearest_work.residual: C1 credit is tied to transport of a controlled persistent-state intervention, not user-controlled personalization dependence

published_nearest_work.work: Demystifying Deep Search: A Holistic Evaluation with Hint-free Multi-Hop Questions and Factorised Metrics
published_nearest_work.overlap: factorized diagnosis separates search sufficiency, knowledge utilization, and refusal; an EvidenceLoop baseline then targets diagnosed weaknesses
published_nearest_work.lesson: for ICLR, diagnosis is substantially stronger when it predicts a concrete intervention or engineering decision rather than stopping at factorized metrics

published_nearest_work.work: AMemGym: Interactive Memory Benchmarking for Assistants in Long-Horizon Conversations
published_nearest_work.overlap: diagnostically rich memory evaluation and optimization in an interactive environment
published_nearest_work.residual: C1 is not a benchmark; its object is controlled transport and stage-specific scientific credit

adjudication.selected_residual_scope: A persistent update receives only the highest stage-specific credit supported by evidence; the first unsupported measured stage generates a repair hypothesis that must be prospectively falsified by a stage-targeted intervention while upstream surfaces are held fixed.
adjudication.why_this_is_not_just_more_metrics: The diagnostic output changes the intervention target: a W+/E-observed/U-not-supported/F+ signature predicts that writer/retrieval work is not the first repair target and instead motivates a controlled post-retrieval policy-integration probe.

venue_fit.ACL: strong fit if the paper combines controlled transport analysis, published-memory comparisons, and a practical stage-indexed credit/repair consequence
venue_fit.ICLR: plausible if the stage signature is shown to predict an actionable repair or boundary, not merely describe where evidence weakens

forbidden_claims: retrieval is not utilization is new
the current exposure-to-uptake evidence boundary is already a causal repair target
the proposed repair probe has improved behavior before it is actually executed and adjudicated
published benchmark/method numbers are directly comparable to C1 unless evaluation protocols are aligned
